_comment: Supersession chain for the frozen closure target. Historical entries are never rewritten -- a target that was superseded is evidence of why, not a mistake to erase. Since adjustment 8 (2026-09-15) a target is superseded only when the PRODUCT identity changes; evidence commits after a target do not supersede it.

chain.why: provisional target pinned before the C-2 corrections; never released. The owner ruled out reusing it.
intermediate target, frozen before the 1.7.0 release commit existed. Superseded within the same session so the target would BE the released revision rather than an ancestor of it.

tagged and pushed under owner approval. The release workflow failed at the release-gate step with four `git archive ... exit 128` errors (D-019); `publish` was skipped and PyPI never received a package. The tag remains on this commit, never moved, deleted or recreated, and its failure artefacts are kept unrewritten at closure-evidence/v1.7.0-release-failure.log and v1.7.0-release-attempt.json.

chain.status: RELEASED -- SUPERSEDED AS CLOSURE TARGET BY 1.7.2 (D-022)
chain.why: the corrected candidate. Carries D-019 (full-history CI checkout), D-020 (two POSIX assumptions in test helpers) and D-021 (pin keys and reported paths normalised to POSIX). Remote CI run 34917002995 is green on exactly this commit across all four Ubuntu suite jobs, Windows, lint and wheel. Superseded 2026-09-15: closure could not converge on it -- recording post-release evidence moved HEAD and G1.0 read FAILED (D-022, a closure-architecture defect, not a product one). The tag and the PyPI artefacts stand unchanged; closure-evidence/releases/1.7.1.json binds them to this commit member by member.

chain.status: RELEASED -- SUPERSEDED AS CLOSURE TARGET BY 1.7.3 (D-026, D-028, D-029)
chain.why: the D-022/D-023 correction: release identity by product digest (aisef/control/planes.py, docs/closure-gate.json#planes), G1.0 comparing product identity between the release and HEAD, G6 bound to a release node with an immutable instructions bundle. Remote CI run 34925033781 green on exactly this commit across Ubuntu 3.11-3.14, Windows 3.11, lint and wheel (the 3.13 job needed one re-run: a temp-dir cleanup race in a bench test helper, D-024, unrelated to the change). The pin commit 25ed1ed sits after this commit and is EVIDENCE_ONLY, which is now allowed. Superseded 2026-09-15: the first dogfood run of the public 1.7.2 package (LedgerLock) found three P1 product defects (closure-evidence/dogfood/ledgerlock/); the product identity moved, as adjustment 8 says it must.

chain.status: RELEASED -- SUPERSEDED AS CLOSURE TARGET BY 1.7.4 (D-032)
chain.why: the D-025…D-031 correction (LedgerLock dogfood intake 2026-09-15): structured-only plan deadlock, harness-built pinned verification image with declared-tool probes, missing runner as UNRUNNABLE with an outcome kind, process-tree kill, coverage artifacts out of scope and candidates, bootstrap grants weighed by the scheduler, orphaned claims named by status. Remote CI run 34966086751 (pull_request, PR #2) green on exactly this commit across Ubuntu 3.11-3.14, Windows 3.11 (Ran 3150 tests, OK, skipped=84, 1503 s), lint and wheel. The previous candidate edcd5ec was REJECTED by the owner: CI run 34959902843 failed one real Windows regression, test_clients turn cap expected 5 turns and observed 6, because the tree kill spawned taskkill (~0.2 s) — cfee273 walks the process snapshot in-process instead. max_turns is a control-plane invariant; the overshoot was not waived.

chain.status: RELEASED -- SUPERSEDED AS CLOSURE TARGET BY 1.7.5 (D-033)
chain.why: the D-032 correction (LedgerLock Run #2 on public 1.7.3, 2026-09-15): a review that did not execute is REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE — the frozen candidate is kept, only the review stage is retried on the same SHA (bounded), a persistent failure ends the story REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE naming the failure, prior review evidence is reused only with a completed verdict, and a resumed story picks up at the review stage; never a developer no-op. Remote CI run 34994305762 (pull_request, PR #3) green on exactly this commit across Ubuntu 3.11-3.14, Windows 3.11 (success — Ran 3163 tests in 1225.771s, OK (skipped=84)), lint and wheel. Nothing else changed in the product plane (narrow patch, owner scope).

the D-033 correction (clean OpenCode replay of LedgerLock Run #2 on public 1.7.4, 2026-09-16): a story's regression baseline is immutable within its epoch — captured once at the integrated parent, reused on retry/resume/verify-only, never the story's own candidate; absent or provenance-invalid baseline fails closed as BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE. Remote CI run 35047338646 (pull_request, PR #4) green on exactly this commit across Ubuntu 3.11-3.14, Windows 3.11 (success — Ran 3177 tests in 1158.202s, OK (skipped=84)), lint and wheel. Nothing else changed in the product plane (narrow patch, owner scope).

defect_chain_note: D-019, D-020 and D-021 form one chain: history-dependent tests could not run at all, which hid two POSIX assumptions in the helpers, which in turn hid a genuine cross-platform product bug in the pin key. Each was only visible once the previous one was fixed. Choosing to fix the environment rather than skip the tests is what surfaced all three.
